item.title: Why Global Visitors Are Flocking to Chinese EVs in Shenzhen?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
From automated parking and tank turns to ultra-fast charging in extreme cold, each technological breakthrough is redefining what's possible in the automotive industry. But beyond the technology itself lies something even more significant: China's innovation speed, R&D capabilities, and industrial strength.
From leading global EV sales to attracting attention from international industry players, China's new energy vehicle sector is making a major leap—from exporting products to expanding its technological influence worldwide.
One car reflects the rise of an entire industry. And what's driving onto the global stage is the strength of Chinese manufacturing and innovation.

item.title: Xi makes four points on how major countries should get along with each other
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday made four points on how major countries should get along with each other and jointly safeguard world peace.
Major countries should uphold mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation, Xi said at a summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province.

item.title: Xi says sound interactions among major countries not an option but a must
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday said that sound interactions among major countries are "not an option but a must."
Xi made the remarks at a summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province.
Xi said major countries bear special responsibilities as people live in the same global village and the fortunes of all countries are intertwined as a community with a shared future.

item.title: Xi says world stability rests upon peace among major countries
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday said peace among major countries brings stability to the world, while their contention would only lead to chaos in the world.
Xi made the remarks at a summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province.
More than 80 years ago, China, Russia and the United States, the key anti-fascist forces in the world, fought shoulder to shoulder and achieved great victories, winning peace and tranquility for the world, Xi said.

item.title: Xi hosts welcome banquet for guests attending APEC meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Chinese President Xi Jinping addresses a welcome banquet in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, on Wednesday hosted a banquet in Shenzhen to welcome guests who are here to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting. (Xinhua/Yao Dawei)
SHENZHEN, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, on Wednesday hosted a banquet in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, to welcome guests who are here to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting.
"I wish to extend, on behalf of the Chinese government and the Chinese people, our warmest welcome to all distinguished guests," Xi said in his toast.
Openness is deeply rooted in Shenzhen's DNA and innovation drives the city's vitality, while cooperation is where its strength comes from, Xi said, adding that the success of Shenzhen is also a microcosm of China's reform and opening up, as well as an example of fruitful cooperation across the Asia-Pacific.
Noting that openness, innovation and cooperation have been the distinctive features of APEC since its establishment, Xi said APEC has grasped the pulse of the times and guided the process of regional economic integration, making the Asia-Pacific the most dynamic region and a vital growth engine of the world economy.
"At tomorrow's Leaders' Meeting, we will discuss steps to expand mutual openness, explore pathways to innovation-driven growth, extend opportunities for result-oriented cooperation across various fields," Xi said.
Before the banquet, Xi and Peng posed for group photos with leaders and representatives from APEC economies and their spouses.
After the banquet, they joined the guests to watch an artistic performance.

item.title: Xi says China-U.S. relations generally stable, positive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with U.S. President Donald Trump, who is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan)
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday said that China-U.S. relations have generally maintained a stable and positive trajectory, injecting stability and certainty into the world.
Xi made the remarks when meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen.
Xi said that he and Trump had jointly explored the right way for China and the United States, as two major countries, to get along, established a new positioning of a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability and given it new meaning based on respect, fairness and reciprocity.
The new positioning has been welcomed by the people of both China and the United States, as well as by the international community, he added.
Xi stressed that building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability is an unprecedented and pioneering endeavor, adding that the key to sustaining the current positive momentum lies in taking concrete action to implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state.
On the Taiwan question, the U.S. side should do the right thing and avoid major disruptions to China-U.S. relations, Xi said.
Trump said he and Xi have jointly guided the development of U.S.-China relations, and both sides should maintain the positive momentum of the stable development in bilateral relations.
The United States does not support "Taiwan independence," Trump said.
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with U.S. President Donald Trump, who is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Tao)

item.title: China is advocate, promoter, forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation: Xi
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
Chinese President Xi Jinping chairs the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and delivers important remarks titled "Building an Asia-Pacific Community and Writing a New Chapter of the Asia-Pacific Miracle" in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu)
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday said China is an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation, and it is ready to work with all parties to build the pillars that support an Asia-Pacific community.
Xi made the remarks at the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held in Shenzhen in south China's Guangdong Province.
Stressing the importance of stronger economic and trade ties underpinning such a community, Xi said efforts should be made to facilitate trade and investment, advance digitalization, and lower barriers to them.
On upgrading connectivity, he called for measures to improve infrastructure networks, enhance coordination in policies and regulations, promote people-to-people exchanges, and foster mutual understanding and closer bonds among peoples.
Emphasizing innovation, Xi said greater efforts need to be made to build digital infrastructure and promote the broad application of artificial intelligence.
Xi stressed the importance of development, calling on regional economies to advance cooperation on energy and food security, anti-corruption governance across borders, and green and low-carbon transition. He also called for efforts to improve the people's well-being and increase investment in human capital.

item.title: Xi Focus: Xi calls for jointly building Asia-Pacific community to prosper together
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 at the Qianhai International Convention Center in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Tao)
SHENZHEN, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged on Wednesday that China is willing to work with all parties to forge ahead with resolve, jointly build an Asia-Pacific community and bring prosperity for all.
Addressing the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 in the southern metropolis of Shenzhen, Xi called on business communities in the region to uphold the entrepreneurial spirit and make greater contributions to economic integration in the Asia-Pacific.
Under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the two-day summit has attracted more than 2,000 representatives from 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies, including Britain, France, Germany and Switzerland.
"The Asia-Pacific is our home; it is here we jointly pursue development and cooperation," Xi said.
Born amid the waves of economic globalization, APEC has been one of the world's most dynamic engines of growth. Today, the APEC economies are home to about 40 percent of the world's population, and account for more than 60 percent of global GDP and nearly half of global trade.
As the world becomes more turbulent and the global economy lacks growth momentum, the Chinese president said the region must answer the "hard questions of our times": to open doors or close doors, work together or against each other, adapt to change or stick to old ways?
In his response, Xi put forward proposals on how the region can prosper together, calling on APEC economies to uphold peace and stability, build bridges of opening up and cooperation, boost innovation to drive growth and expand ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes.
All parties in the region must "uphold the postwar international order," he said, calling on them to resolve differences through dialogue and consultation and address challenges through solidarity and coordination.
Xi said the Asia-Pacific should support free and open trade and investment while keeping the global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded.
"History tells us that opening doors brings progress while closing doors leaves one behind," he said, calling for efforts to steadily advance the process of the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific.
He stressed the need to forge partnerships in science, technology and innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence, and promote green and low-carbon development.
"By doing so, we can turn strengths in innovation into drivers of growth, and provide strong impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific," the president said.
The region should also remove trade and investment barriers to build an open Asia-Pacific economy, and promote development that is balanced and delivers benefits to all to ensure both efficiency and fairness, Xi said.
According to Xi, there is much to draw from the success of Shenzhen, host of this year's APEC CEO Summit and the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting.
Over the past 40 years and more, Shenzhen has been a pioneer in China's pursuit of reform and opening up. It has achieved a historic transformation from a small border town into an international metropolis, creating a miracle in the history of global development, Xi said.
Noting that the Asia-Pacific region is home to the world's most important bay areas notable for their open and interconnected economies with positive spillover effects, Xi said China supports the establishment of a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation to deepen exchanges and interactions among bay areas from across the world.
"This will help us explore new ways for stronger economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific," he said.
Looking ahead, as China's ties with the Asia-Pacific grow increasingly close, Xi said China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) provides a list of opportunities for promoting economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and the wider world.
The development blueprint is "an invitation for cooperation China has sent to business communities from around the world," he said.
Xi said China will provide the global business community with a super-sized open market, a promising land for development, as well as an environment that enables mutually reinforcing cooperation.
He highlighted China's accelerating efforts to develop a big, open market and build a modern industrial system, pledging a more stable and predictable first-class environment for companies from around the world to invest and do business in China.
Calling the Asia-Pacific business communities "pioneers of the global economy," he said they are "more than welcome to continue to get actively involved in China's reform and opening up and modernization drive, and share in the opportunities created by Chinese modernization."
Leaders of APEC economies, including Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, attended the summit.
Having previously hosted the APEC Economic Leaders' Meetings in 2001 and 2014, China is taking on the role of APEC host for the third time this year. It has hosted more than 300 APEC meetings and events this year and reached nearly 50 practical outcomes with other APEC economies in the economic and trade field.
